name: Ty Segall
label: Drag City
lede: A Laguna Beach surf kid who made three albums in 2012 alone, drummed in a hard rock band on the side, toured in a baby mask, and has barely stopped releasing records since.

eras.title: Filmed for MTV, playing garage rock
eras.text: Segall grew up in Laguna Beach, surfing from age ten, adopted by a lawyer father and an artist mother. Music came in high school with Mikal Cronin and a string of bands, then a move north to San Francisco, where John Dwyer of Thee Oh Sees gave him his first proper album release.

years.h: Ty Segall is born in Laguna Beach, California
years.p: Segall is adopted; his father is a lawyer and his mother an artist. He starts surfing at ten.

years.h: MTV's Laguna Beach films at Ty Segall's high school
years.p: The reality show Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County shoots at Segall's school from 2005 to 2007. His band would later mock it on video.

years.cap: Ty Segall and the Freedom Band, 2021 · Wikimedia
years.h: Epsilons make a parody of Laguna Beach
years.p: Segall's grunge band [[Epsilons|6024a330-a8af-42e9-a923-fe7d1026dd28]], with his high school friend [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]], films a send-up of the MTV show that had been shooting at their school.
years.xp: Segall cycled through bands in these years: [[The Traditional Fools|59897dd7-28bf-4922-9867-c46b5983d240]], Party Fowl, [[Sic Alps|c6f39f9e-b0fc-4614-94a9-ecf648bd8f33]] and Evil Robots among them. Cronin was also in Party Fowl and [[Moonhearts|e35c28f4-ead4-465d-9d99-6bbf8ad7f018]].

years.h: Ty Segall finishes college and builds grow boxes
years.p: After a media studies degree at the University of San Francisco, Segall spends eight months building boxes for growing cannabis.

years.h: Horn the Unicorn on cassette
years.p: Segall's first solo tape comes out on the small Wizard Mountain label, followed by a split cassette with Superstitions.

years.h: Ty Segall, the debut on Castle Face
years.p: [[John Dwyer|8d941959-2af3-447d-aa39-a215057ae7f5]] of Thee Oh Sees befriends Segall and puts out his first album on Castle Face Records, Dwyer's label.

eras.title: Three albums in one year
eras.text: Segall made records faster than most bands book tours: two for Memphis's Goner, a jump to Drag City, and then 2012, when he put out a collaboration, a band record and a solo album inside twelve months.

years.h: Lemons on Goner Records
years.p: Segall's second album comes out on Goner, the Memphis garage label.

years.h: Reverse Shark Attack with Mikal Cronin
years.p: Segall and [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]] release a joint album: a cassette on Burger Records and vinyl on Kill Shaman.

years.h: Melted, the last Goner album
years.p: Segall's third album, and his last before signing to Drag City.

years.h: Goodbye Bread: Ty Segall's first for Drag City
years.p: Written over six months in producer Eric Bauer's basement and recorded at Fantasy Studios in San Francisco. Segall calls it the most serious album he has made.
years.xp: Sessions ran from June 2010 to January 2011. Critics heard him slowing down: AllMusic's Mark Deming wrote that he was mellowing out just a bit. Pitchfork put it at No. 31 on its 2011 list.

years.h: Charles Moothart starts Fuzz with Ty Segall on drums
years.p: [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] wonders how hard it would be to write a hard rock song, shows Segall the result, and [[Fuzz|1625819f-79d7-4787-b2fb-0e0c260bac85]] is born, with Segall singing from behind the kit.

years.h: Hair, with Tim Presley's White Fence
years.p: The first Segall collaboration with [[Tim Presley|25f6404b-4738-48a2-b1e0-465b7430fb93]] of [[White Fence|68548de4-c045-426a-9745-b52a8a22d2d2]], on Drag City. They reunite for Joy in 2018.

years.h: Slaughterhouse by the Ty Segall Band
years.p: A loud full-band record on In the Red, with [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]] on bass, [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] on guitar and Emily Rose Epstein on drums.

years.h: Twins makes three Ty Segall albums in 2012
years.p: After Hair and Slaughterhouse, Segall's solo Twins comes out on Drag City. He said he wanted evil space rock.
years.xp: The three 2012 records were on two labels under three billings: Ty Segall and White Fence, the Ty Segall Band, and Ty Segall alone. Most bands take longer than that to make one.

eras.title: A death, an acoustic record, then fourteen months on one album
eras.text: Segall's father died, and he became estranged from his mother. He answered with the quiet, acoustic Sleeper, then spent more than a year on Manipulator, the first of his albums to reach the Billboard 200.

years.h: Sleeper: Ty Segall's acoustic album after his father's death
years.p: Recorded January to March 2013 in San Francisco, after the death of his father, Brian. The song Crazy addresses his estrangement from his mother.
years.xp:
Segall said he was not in a good spot, with his father gone and relationship trouble on top. He thought the songs were demos until they turned into the album.

For the tour he put together the Sleeper Band: Sean Paul on guitar, Andrew Luttrell on bass, [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] on drums.

years.h: Fuzz, the debut, with Ty Segall on drums
years.p: [[Fuzz|1625819f-79d7-4787-b2fb-0e0c260bac85]]'s first album comes out with [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] on guitar and Roland Cosio on bass. Chad Ubovich later takes over bass.

years.h: Manipulator takes 14 months and hits the Billboard 200
years.p: Co-produced with [[Chris Woodhouse|cb9a3eab-d598-4977-ae54-1e85d4529b1a]], who also recorded and mixed it. Manipulator peaks at No. 45, Segall's first time on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Ty Segall signs Wand to his GOD? label
years.p: Through GOD?, his imprint at Drag City, Segall signs the Los Angeles band Wand and takes them on tour.

eras.title: A baby mask and the Freedom Band
eras.text: Segall moved to Los Angeles and made his strangest record, then his most live-sounding ones. Steve Albini recorded a band that became the Freedom Band, and the albums got longer.

years.h: Emotional Mugger and a baby-masked alter ego
years.p: Segall tours Emotional Mugger with the Muggers, often wearing a baby mask and going by Sloppo. He announced the album by sending out a VHS tape.
years.xp: The Muggers were [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]], [[Emmett Kelly|81169a01-84eb-46e2-83af-f6bda1e0da5c]], Kyle Thomas, [[Cory Hanson|cf2f8c4f-00ae-41c9-91b7-294b2747c11a]] of Wand and Evan Burrows. Reviews split: The Guardian called it a bad trip rather than a mellow high.

q: He just wants to help you make what you want to make.
years.h: A second Ty Segall, recorded live by Steve Albini
years.p: The band plays live in the room for [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. Warm Hands (Freedom Return) runs over ten minutes, and the single Orange Color Queen is about Denée, his girlfriend.
years.xp: Segall on Albini: There's no ego. The players, [[Emmett Kelly|81169a01-84eb-46e2-83af-f6bda1e0da5c]], [[Mikal Cronin|c1a217e0-4b3e-46d7-9613-6a14c9e70895]], [[Charles Moothart|9478d424-3514-4cf8-abd0-12ec65dea921]] and Ben Boye, became known as the Freedom Band.

years.h: Ty Segall writes a TV theme for Jordan Klepper
years.p: Segall composes the theme for Comedy Central's The Opposition with Jordan Klepper, and in 2018 for the series Corporate.

years.h: Freedom's Goblin: 19 songs, opening with one for his dog
years.p: Nearly 75 minutes from four studios, most engineered by [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. It opens with Fanny Dog, about his dog, and covers Hot Chocolate's Every 1's a Winner.
years.xp: Segall said the theme was the anti-theme, the point being to be free. [[Fred Armisen|b1bad7e7-18fd-4c1d-9a64-66c3696209ac]] guests, and Denée Segall sings lead on one track and took photos. It closes with the 12-minute And, Goodnight.

eras.title: No guitars, a home studio, and still no slowing
eras.text: Into his thirties Segall kept testing rules: an album with no guitars, a synth record made in his own studio, an acoustic one at home, an instrumental one for percussion. He added side bands too, from GØGGS to Wasted Shirt with Brian Chippendale.

years.h: First Taste: a Ty Segall album with no guitars
years.p: Segall, known first as a guitarist, makes a whole album without one.

years.h: Wasted Shirt: Ty Segall and Brian Chippendale
years.p: Segall and [[Lightning Bolt|978a36f7-85c6-44ca-a02e-7564e8fa8284]] drummer [[Brian Chippendale|2de5109e-2713-46dd-8de5-f64ee000da49]] release Fungus II as [[Wasted Shirt|bcba7375-6862-4636-888b-00c486c8b959]].

years.h: III, Fuzz's third album
years.p: [[Fuzz|1625819f-79d7-4787-b2fb-0e0c260bac85]] return, with Segall still behind the drums and the single Returning out in July.

years.h: Harmonizer, made in Ty Segall's own studio
years.p: Co-produced by [[Cooper Crain|889452cf-b293-480d-9b1d-1959490530c7]], with Segall's wife Denée Segall featured. It's named for his Los Angeles studio.

years.h: Hello, Hi, recorded in Ty Segall's home studio
years.p: A mostly quiet, acoustic record, made at home.

years.h: Three Bells, Ty Segall's fifteenth album
years.p: A long, knotty Drag City record that critics welcomed.

years.h: Ty Segall sings Animals Are Sleeping on Yo Gabba Gabbaland!
years.p: Segall performs a lullaby on the children's show's revival.

years.h: Love Rudiments, an instrumental album
years.p: Months after Three Bells, Segall releases a second 2024 album, entirely instrumental.

years.h: Possession, Ty Segall's seventeenth album
years.p: Another year, another record.

years.h: Chrome arrives in August 2026
years.p: Segall's newest album, after a January EP of BBC sessions.
